newsitem.title: UK: Welcome Break FRNs to have 10 and 13-yr maturities.
newsitem.headline: Welcome Break FRNs to have 10 and 13-yr maturities.

text.p: The floating rate notes (FRNs) being planned by INVESTCORP's Welcome Break as part of a 320 million stg transaction will have maturities of 10 and 13 years, a banker at Chase Manhattan, one of the joint lead managers, said on Friday.
A report in the Financial Times newspaper said the FRNs would have maturities of 10 and 30 years.
Welcome Break, a chain of motorway service stations in Britain, was expected to raise around 320 million stg via a mix of fixed and floating-rate bonds in the near future.
There will be around 210 million stg of fixed-rate paper in two tranches with maturities of about 20 years.
The balance will be in the 10- and 13-year FRNs.

The bonds will be backed by cash flows from Welcome Break's operations. Proceeds will repay loans taken out when Bahrain-based INVESTCORP paid Granada Group 476 million stg for Welcome Break in February.
Bankers Trust will be the other joint lead manager.
BZW will be a co-lead manager.
